checks.claim: The Mercedes S-Class's optional rear-axle steering turns the rear wheels up to 10 degrees, which cuts the turning circle by up to about 2 meters (the base system is 4.5 degrees)
checks.why: Sources support 10 degrees and a roughly 2 m (6.5 ft) reduction, but both are 'up to' figures and 10 degrees is the optional larger system; the base system is 4.5 degrees.

checks.claim: Honda offered four-wheel steering on its Prelude from 1987
checks.why: Honda's tech site says it introduced 4WS in the Prelude in 1987 as an option, and a 1987 UPI road test confirms it. Avoid saying 'first ever'.

checks.claim: Some rear-steer systems, such as BMW's Integral Active Steering and one DAF truck rear axle, are designed so a fault leaves the rear wheels centred or straight
checks.why: Evidence is limited to a DAF case study and a parts-retailer page on BMW; no general rule and no Mercedes source, so it can't be claimed for all systems or the S-Class.
